surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Texier wins it in a shootout
paras: Olen Zellweger, who scores in about 1 game in 11, scored twice. Zellweger scored his first goal for Buffalo early in the first to open the scoring, but Lane Hutson made it 1-1 for Montréal on the power play midway through the period. Cole Caufield put the Canadiens up 2-1 early in the second. Josh Anderson made it 3-1 late in the period. Josh Norris and Zellweger scored just over a minute apart early in the third to tie it 3-3. Caufield, Alexandre Texier and Zachary Bolduc scored in the shootout for the Canadiens.

The Canadiens outshot the Sabres 38-16, but the Sabres’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Jacob Fowler made 13 saves for the Canadiens, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 35 of 38 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Juraj Slafkovský, by our Swing measure.
The Canadiens killed all five Sabres power plays. The Habs improved to 3-2-1 and took fifth place in the Atlantic from the Sabres, who fell to 3-3-1.

items.text: Nick Suzuki extended his point streak against Buffalo to nine games.
With Rasmus Dahlin out, Zellweger took his spot and scored twice.
Josh Norris scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 15.
The Canadiens beat the Sabres in seven games in last spring’s second round.
